inputs.original_text: Concerns are mounting over proposed changes to Cyprus’ surveillance legislation, particularly efforts to remove judicial oversight as a key safeguard, lawyers said on Monday. The amended bill is expected to be brought before the House plenum for a vote on Thursday. According to Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides, following a recent closed session of the House [...]
inputs.modified_text: This is a power grab dressed up as legal reform. They’re pushing changes to Cyprus’ surveillance law that would remove judicial oversight, with a House vote expected Thursday—and the fact it was discussed in a closed session tells you how much they want scrutiny kept out of sight. Lawyers are warning about it, but the people steering this clearly see accountability as an obstacle. The secrecy isn’t incidental; it’s part of the plan.
